gate: No new innovation gameplay implementation until combined first 20 ideas reviewed, then 200 additional unique concepts fully specified and cross-deduplicated; 220 total.

concepts.title: Causality Loom — explainable world consequence director
concepts.novelty_audit: Current quests are static counters and festivals fixed-date; this is a player-readable event graph with bounded competing consequences, not a second festival calendar or construction stage system.
concepts.player_scenario: Two dry days forecast a pollinator shortage. At the meadow noticeboard the player can plant flowers, request help, or defer; each choice visibly changes habitat and the following week's market.
player_loop: Two dry days forecast a pollinator shortage. At the meadow noticeboard the player can plant flowers, request help, or defer; each choice visibly changes habitat and the following week's market. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Event prerequisites, exclusivity, priority, cooldown and seed ordering are immutable; evaluate once per monotonic day_epoch and limit to eight activations per dawn.
Preview is read-only. Command IDs are idempotent; choice and effects share one receipt, with deferred events retried fairly.
A missing domain effect adapter rejects activation without silently changing farm or village state.
service_contracts: Principal calendar/save authority; Farming/Village read-only predicates and idempotent domain effect adapters; independent event journal.
Never mutate game.gd, farm.gd or village.gd without owner-approved adapter and assembled-save regression.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Click cause cards, arrows navigate choices, Enter commits, Esc postpones.
controls.gamepad: D-pad navigates event graph, A selects, B exits, shoulders move timeline.
controls.touch: Tap large cause nodes, swipe consequence timeline, explicit accept/postpone controls.

original_asset_plan: Original inked weather glyphs, pressed-flower event cards and legible causal arrows.
Original short chimes and low-motion environmental overlays with accessible text explanations.

performance_budget.desktop: Up to 256 definitions and eight activations per dawn, deterministic evaluation target <2ms CPU; journal paging 32 cards.
performance_budget.mobile: Up to 128 active regional definitions and 16 visible cards, target <4ms CPU per dawn, never per-frame scanning.

godot_acceptance: Two seeded runs choose identical eligible events and priority order.
Duplicate choice command changes one resource receipt and one journal entry.
Winter year-one to Spring year-two save/reload preserves monotonic cooldowns and causal history.
adversarial_tests: Reject cyclic prerequisite graph, unknown choice, negative cooldown, invalid domain delta and reentrant event.
Stress 500 eligible events: eight activate, remainder defer without event storm or starvation.
concepts.engine_portability: JSON event DAG, integer epochs and effect receipts are engine-neutral; Godot noticeboard is a view adapter, Unreal/Unity later require independent parity tests.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Preview and postponement consume nothing; accepted planting consumes exactly two seeds once and failure leaves inventory unchanged.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: No B-003 building stages, B-008 construction labor or B-010 housing simulation.
implementation_phases: Pure deterministic domain rules and JSON schema plus mutation tests after 220 gate.
Godot adapter and original visual feedback plus native acceptance after 220 gate.
Cross-domain assembled-save regression, controller/touch parity and device performance measurement before release.

concepts.title: Riverglass Accord — watershed habitat and fish migration
concepts.novelty_audit: Current lake fishing awards a fish, and Farming F02 handles crop-bed moisture. This models regional water quality and migratory fish connectivity, not B-004 roof rainwater capture.
concepts.player_scenario: A silted tributary blocks silverfin spawning. The player samples three sites, plants reeds and proposes a seasonal catch limit; shoals and market supply respond across seasons.
player_loop: A silted tributary blocks silverfin spawning. The player samples three sites, plants reeds and proposes a seasonal catch limit; shoals and market supply respond across seasons. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Directed segment graph tracks bounded water quality 0..100 and integer fish population; migration conserves fish except explicit births, deaths and catch.
Turbidity changes after elapsed days and upstream signals; no instant habitat repair. Farm runoff is read-only external input.
Once-per-epoch catch receipts prevent repeated harvest; low population enforces clear no-catch recovery.
service_contracts: Farming hydrology supplies bounded runoff summary; Valley owns sample markers; Principal saves river state.
Village market may consume sustainable fish signal but cannot independently mint fish stock.

controls.mouse_keyboard: E samples at river markers, mouse selects restoration choice on watershed map.
controls.gamepad: A samples, D-pad compares segments, shoulders select restoration option.
controls.touch: Tap marked sample post, use large site cards and explicit restore/cancel buttons.

original_asset_plan: Original shoal silhouettes, reed meshes and low-poly riverbank detail.
Original sample-vial icons, sediment gradients and calm river audio with color-independent labels.

performance_budget.desktop: At most 24 river segments and 12 fish cohorts; dawn model target <2ms CPU and pooled shoal visuals.
performance_budget.mobile: At most 12 rendered segments, 40 pooled fish proxies and <4ms CPU per dawn; no fluid physics.

godot_acceptance: A three-segment migration conserves exactly 100 fish before explicit births/catch.
Planting reeds improves quality after seven dawns, not immediately.
Reload after year rollover preserves cohorts, catch limits and survey history.
adversarial_tests: Reject cyclic downstream graph, negative fish, nonexistent site, duplicate catch and exceeding stock.
Missing runoff adapter freezes the affected segment with a visible unavailable reason; no fabricated water.
concepts.engine_portability: Integer river graph and conservation ledger portable; Godot MultiMesh fish and shoreline shader are replaceable views.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Sample is free; planting debits three seeds only after valid commit; duplicates and failed actions cannot charge again.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: Not B-004 rainroof plumbing, B-002 terrain foundations or Farm's soil moisture model.
implementation_phases: Pure deterministic domain rules and JSON schema plus mutation tests after 220 gate.
Godot adapter and original visual feedback plus native acceptance after 220 gate.
Cross-domain assembled-save regression, controller/touch parity and device performance measurement before release.

concepts.title: Lantern Letters — consent-based promises and verifiable village stories
concepts.novelty_audit: Village already has affection and saved resident memory. This adds provenance, confidentiality, delivery and recoverable promise consequences across NPCs, not another gift/affection score.
concepts.player_scenario: A baker asks the player to deliver a sealed letter. The recipient may decline, ask for evidence or respond; the player's respect for privacy changes later invitations.
player_loop: A baker asks the player to deliver a sealed letter. The recipient may decline, ask for evidence or respond; the player's respect for privacy changes later invitations. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Each letter records issuer, recipient, consent scope, deadline epoch and stable receipt; private claims never spread without consent.
Late delivery offers apology/recovery, not permanent social softlock. Only approved Village interface changes targeted relationship state.
Duplicate delivery commands are no-ops even after save/reload and across a year boundary.
service_contracts: Village owns NPC identities, schedules, affinity and consent; Principal owns calendar/save.
Narrative ledger owns letter and claim provenance; no direct modification to village.gd without owner coordination.

controls.mouse_keyboard: E talks to issuer/recipient, number keys choose options, R opens promise journal.
controls.gamepad: A talks/selects, shoulders show promise journal, B declines disclosure.
controls.touch: Tap conversation bubble and large verify/deliver/return cards with clear privacy status.

original_asset_plan: Original sealed lantern envelopes, mailbox props and paper journal art.
Original page Foley and readable character reaction icons with verified provenance.

performance_budget.desktop: Up to 128 active promises, 256 evidence edges and 32 visible cards, expiry target <1ms/day.
performance_budget.mobile: Up to 64 active promises and 16 cards, paginated text, expiry target <2ms/day.

godot_acceptance: Consenting delivery modifies only intended NPC trust exactly once.
Declined disclosure does not propagate claim to unrelated residents.
Deadline from year one does not reset on year-two Spring and apology remains possible.
adversarial_tests: Reject forged consent, unknown NPC, duplicate receipt, self-delivery loop and revoked visibility.
Reject malformed legacy letter without mutating current save or NPC relationship.
concepts.engine_portability: Portable consent/provenance graph and receipts; dialogue and mailbox are Godot views only.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Basic courier errand is free; optional stipend is paid once on accepted receipt, never on canceled preview.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: Not B-005 spatial room memory, B-007 blueprint plans or B-008 building labor.
implementation_phases: Pure deterministic domain rules and JSON schema plus mutation tests after 220 gate.
Godot adapter and original visual feedback plus native acceptance after 220 gate.
Cross-domain assembled-save regression, controller/touch parity and device performance measurement before release.

concepts.title: Wayfarer Pulse — weather-aware caravan logistics and bounded markets
concepts.novelty_audit: Existing village shops/jobs are local transactions. This adds finite itinerant stock, route risk and escrowed reservations, not B-008 NPC construction labor.
concepts.player_scenario: Mist delays a mountain caravan. The player escorts the shipment, substitutes local produce or postpones a feast, with visible stock and price consequences.
player_loop: Mist delays a mountain caravan. The player escorts the shipment, substitutes local produce or postpones a feast, with visible stock and price consequences. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Caravan manifests have finite integer stock and seeded arrival epochs; one caravan cannot occupy two towns at once.
Escrow gold or goods once, never both; cancellation refunds by published bounded policy; delivery receipts cannot be duplicated.
Price multiplier remains 50..175 percent of base, and severe weather always has a recoverable alternative route.
service_contracts: Village shop provides baseline prices, Farming crop availability, Principal inventory/gold authority.
EventDirector announces disruptions, while caravan scheduler owns unique route instances.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Click village route map, arrow keys set quantity, Enter reserves and E greets arrival.
controls.gamepad: D-pad selects route, stick sets quantity, A confirms and B cancels.
controls.touch: Tap route card, quantity stepper, large reserve/cancel and readable receipt.

original_asset_plan: Original wagon silhouettes, stamped cargo cards and painted map routes.
Original wheels-and-bells audio and weather-delay icons.

performance_budget.desktop: Up to 12 caravans, 32 routes and 256 reservations, dawn update <1ms CPU.
performance_budget.mobile: Up to six rendered merchants and 12 visible route cards, dawn update <2ms CPU.

godot_acceptance: Reservation charges escrow once and delivery credits exact stock once.
Rain delay changes arrival deterministically without duplicate wagon spawn.
Cancellation and reload return correct escrow and clear pending shipment.
adversarial_tests: Reject negative quantity, stale quote, insufficient funds, unknown route and duplicate settlement.
No route remains permanently blocked after bounded severe-weather cycles.
concepts.engine_portability: Integer route and escrow ledgers portable; Godot map/merchant visuals are adapters.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Before dispatch cancel returns full escrow; later refund follows a bounded quoted policy; rejected or duplicate command changes no balances.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: Not B-008 construction contracts or B-009 structural salvage.
implementation_phases: Pure deterministic domain rules and JSON schema plus mutation tests after 220 gate.
Godot adapter and original visual feedback plus native acceptance after 220 gate.
Cross-domain assembled-save regression, controller/touch parity and device performance measurement before release.

concepts.title: Starpath Almanac — fictional sky navigation and multi-route mysteries
concepts.novelty_audit: The current highlands have static wayfinding signs, not astronomical clue navigation. This is an inference puzzle tied to seasonal observations, not cosmetic weather or terrain construction.
concepts.player_scenario: On an autumn evening, the player rotates a carved star wheel against mountain silhouettes to reveal a hidden herb grove; winter mist offers an alternate grounded clue.
player_loop: On an autumn evening, the player rotates a carved star wheel against mountain silhouettes to reveal a hidden herb grove; winter mist offers an alternate grounded clue. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Celestial bearings are fictional, deterministic by seed, season and region, and do not purport to be real navigation.
Each mystery has two independently accessible clue routes and optional hints; poor weather cannot permanently block completion.
One mystery completion yields one unique reward receipt; later visits yield lore only.
service_contracts: Principal supplies season/weather/time, Valley supplies safe landmarks, Village optional clues.
Principal inventory owns unique reward and save; sky shader never decides gameplay results.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Drag star wheel with mouse, Q/E fine nudges, M opens clues, Enter records bearing.
controls.gamepad: Right stick rotates wheel, triggers nudge, A records and shoulder swaps clues.
controls.touch: One-finger rotate wheel, visible nudge buttons, high-contrast bearing and optional auto-align.

original_asset_plan: Original night sky glyphs, carved wooden star wheel and skyline silhouettes.
Original soft chimes and low-particle mobile night-sky alternative.

performance_budget.desktop: At most 120 sky points and 16 clue markers, sky calculation <1ms CPU, one cached star map.
performance_budget.mobile: At most 64 sky points, no volumetric sky effects, calculation <2ms CPU at 30fps tier.

godot_acceptance: Same seed/year/season yields identical bearings and clue IDs.
Mist blocks sky route but ground clue still resolves mystery.
Reload and year rollover cannot grant mystery reward twice.
adversarial_tests: Reject NaN angle, unknown clue, invalid region and duplicate reward.
Missing landmark adapter must not teleport player or mutate unrelated world state.
concepts.engine_portability: Integer bearings and clue state portable; Godot sky shader/camera is replaceable.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Observation and hints cost no scarce items; completion reward uses a single idempotent receipt.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: No B-002 terrain sculpting, B-003 house phases or B-010 home climate.
implementation_phases: Pure deterministic domain rules and JSON schema plus mutation tests after 220 gate.
Godot adapter and original visual feedback plus native acceptance after 220 gate.
Cross-domain assembled-save regression, controller/touch parity and device performance measurement before release.

concepts.title: Wildsign Atlas — ethical wildlife migration and companion tracking
concepts.novelty_audit: Barn animal care exists, but no nonviolent regional wildlife sign tracking. This models migratory cohorts, tracks and optional companion hints, not livestock production.
concepts.player_scenario: Follow seasonal hoofprints from the woods to the highlands, set a harmless observation hide and ask a trusted companion to locate a distant herd without capturing animals.
player_loop: Follow seasonal hoofprints from the woods to the highlands, set a harmless observation hide and ask a trusted companion to locate a distant herd without capturing animals. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Wildlife cohort population and waypoint route are stable, bounded and updated once per day; rendered agents are a subset of aggregate state.
Tracks expire after one to three epochs, sightings credit once per species/season/region, and observation never harms wildlife.
Companion assistance is optional and cannot lock out players without companions; fallback hints remain available.
service_contracts: Valley supplies spawn-safe regions, Farming Animals remains barn-only, Principal owns save.
Optional companion adapter supplies trust; event director consumes sightings as read-only triggers.

controls.mouse_keyboard: E inspects tracks, R opens atlas, click evidence cards and C asks companion.
controls.gamepad: A inspects, shoulder opens atlas, D-pad compares tracks, X asks companion.
controls.touch: Tap footprint glyph, large evidence cards and explicit companion hint button.

original_asset_plan: Original low-poly fantasy wildlife silhouettes, tracks and hide marker.
Original forest rustle audio and reduced-motion directional clue overlays.

performance_budget.desktop: At most eight visible wildlife agents and 96 track decals; daily migration <2ms CPU.
performance_budget.mobile: At most three rendered agents and 24 decals, offscreen simulation integer-only <3ms/day.

godot_acceptance: Season changes move cohort to next waypoint without losing animals.
Repeated sighting and reload grant one journal discovery.
No companion still permits every essential observation via manual clues.
adversarial_tests: Reject negative cohort, expired track, impossible observation distance and duplicate receipt.
No agent may spawn inside solid geometry or water; failed placement must preserve state.
concepts.engine_portability: Cohort graph and sightings are portable; Godot animation/pathfinding need new adapters after port.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Hide preview costs nothing, commit debits materials once, and dismantle returns bounded salvage without duplication.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: Observation hide is a simple marker, not B-001 socket building or B-010 house construction.
implementation_phases: Pure deterministic domain rules and JSON schema plus mutation tests after 220 gate.
Godot adapter and original visual feedback plus native acceptance after 220 gate.
Cross-domain assembled-save regression, controller/touch parity and device performance measurement before release.

concepts.title: Tradition Seedbank — community-authored evolving celebrations
concepts.novelty_audit: Village currently has fixed original festival dates and rewards. This introduces player-proposed rituals, NPC consent and year-over-year traditions without replacing fixed festival logic.
concepts.player_scenario: Propose next spring's lantern procession theme, invite musicians and choose a daytime route; residents remember who participated and may change next year's ceremony.
player_loop: Propose next spring's lantern procession theme, invite musicians and choose a daytime route; residents remember who participated and may change next year's ceremony. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Every proposal has stable ID, consent votes and a single annual occurrence; residents can opt out without penalty.
Existing four festivals keep calendar priority; conflicting rituals receive alternative dates or smaller fallback gathering.
Hosting is once per year and contribution materials are debited exactly once after schedule approval.
service_contracts: Village owns resident schedules, consent and fixed festival calendar; Farming supplies optional flowers.
Principal owns time/save; no edits to festivals.gd until Village authorizes new adapter.

controls.mouse_keyboard: E opens community board, arrows choose theme and venue, Enter invites or hosts.
controls.gamepad: D-pad selects cards, A proposes, B cancels, shoulder opens history.
controls.touch: Tap large theme cards and invite/host controls, readable vote tally.

original_asset_plan: Original lantern ribbons, garlands and paper-cut festival motifs.
Original instrumental loops and subtitle-ready community announcements.

performance_budget.desktop: Up to 16 traditions, 64 annual receipts and 24 pooled crowd silhouettes, scheduling <2ms/day.
performance_budget.mobile: At most 12 crowd proxies and 16 traditions; simplified lighting, scheduling <3ms/day.

godot_acceptance: Rejected proposal offers optional smaller ritual without replacing fixed festival.
Approved theme and opt-outs persist into year two with one occurrence.
Conflicting rituals choose alternate date and do not duplicate celebration.
adversarial_tests: Reject duplicate host, invalid vote, nonexistent NPC and invalid 56-day calendar date.
Legacy save missing traditions loads safely and retains existing festivals.
concepts.engine_portability: Proposal/vote/calendar state portable; Godot procession and audio are replaceable views.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Proposal and votes cost nothing; successful hosting consumes two flowers once; failed hosting returns all reservations.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: Unlike B-008 Village Build Commons, this is a social ritual, not NPC construction.

concepts.title: Pattern Orchard — authored textile motifs and maker exchange
concepts.novelty_audit: Crafting currently has fixed recipes; Builder blueprints concern architecture. This lets players weave original bounded pattern grids and exchange crafted fabrics, not house plans.
concepts.player_scenario: Blend two farm-grown dyes, weave a scarf motif on a loom, then enter it into a village exhibition where NPC tastes affect limited demand.
player_loop: Blend two farm-grown dyes, weave a scarf motif on a loom, then enter it into a village exhibition where NPC tastes affect limited demand. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Pattern is an 8x8 integer grid with at most six palette colors; no user-supplied scripts or copied external images.
Preview never debits resources. Craft consumes fiber/dye once and creates an item with stable pattern snapshot.
Market demand is bounded and buyback cannot generate instant unlimited currency.
service_contracts: Farming supplies dye plants/fiber, Village consumes exhibition entries, Principal owns inventory and money.
Renderer derives texture from integer pattern; do not import unlicensed design graphics.

controls.mouse_keyboard: Click loom cells, drag dye swatches, Ctrl+Z undo, Enter crafts.
controls.gamepad: D-pad selects cell, A paints, shoulders change palette, X previews.
controls.touch: Tap enlarged grid, numbered swatches and visible undo/commit controls.

original_asset_plan: Original generated weave textures and botanical swatches.
Original carved loom and shuttle Foley with colorblind-friendly patterns.

performance_budget.desktop: At most 128 patterns and 64x64 cached preview per visible item; regenerate only on edit.
performance_budget.mobile: At most 32 visible previews, 32x32 textures and no per-frame regeneration.

godot_acceptance: Identical grid and dyes produce identical render key and properties.
One craft consumes exact fiber and dye inputs; preview/cancel cost nothing.
Exhibition entry and sale issue one receipt across save/reload.
adversarial_tests: Reject grid larger than 8x8, invalid palette, missing dye and duplicate item instance.
Deleted pattern must not orphan crafted item's immutable pattern snapshot.
concepts.engine_portability: Integer grids and palette IDs portable; Godot ImageTexture generated as a view.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Commit consumes one fiber and two plants only if valid; canceled design consumes nothing; sold item removed before payout.

concepts.cross_loop_boundary: Not B-007 house blueprints, B-010 interior decorating or B-009 salvage.
implementation_phases: Pure deterministic domain rules and JSON schema plus mutation tests after 220 gate.

concepts.title: Mistwake Passage — accessible canoe routes and hidden wetlands
concepts.novelty_audit: Lake currently serves fishing with static water geometry. This adds safe route planning, paddling and accessible alternate paths, not construction foundations or roof plumbing.
concepts.player_scenario: A mist bank closes a direct canoe route. The player follows floating markers along a slower shoreline path to a herb island, with optional autopaddle for touch users.
player_loop: A mist bank closes a direct canoe route. The player follows floating markers along a slower shoreline path to a herb island, with optional autopaddle for touch users. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: Water routes form finite graph with depth/current/weather constraints; no teleport or crossing impassable terrain.
Each accepted edge charges bounded stamina once; interrupted load restores last safe mooring without lost inventory.
Critical destinations have an alternate assisted or walking route; no frame-perfect control requirement.
service_contracts: Valley owns lake geometry, Principal player position/stamina/save, exploration journal owns discovered routes.
No modification to valley.gd or player controller before explicit interface agreement.

controls.mouse_keyboard: WASD paddles, M opens route map, E moors, Shift toggles assisted mode.
controls.gamepad: Left stick paddles, A moors, shoulder cycles waypoint, X toggles assist.
controls.touch: Two large paddle controls or one-tap waypoint autopaddle, clear moor/stop buttons.

original_asset_plan: Original carved canoe, painted depth ripples and floating route lanterns.
Original water-lap audio and low-motion camera alternative.

performance_budget.desktop: At most 24 water edges, one canoe proxy and 16 pooled ripples; path solve <1ms CPU.
performance_budget.mobile: At most 12 visible edges, four ripples and kinematic canoe; path solve <2ms CPU.

godot_acceptance: Shallow route rejects canoe and offers valid alternative.
Duplicate route command charges stamina once and reload restores safe state.
Assist mode reaches every essential destination without timing challenge.
adversarial_tests: Reject unknown mooring, negative energy, invalid progress and duplicate edge receipt.
On interrupted scene load, recover to safe mooring and conserve all inventory.
concepts.engine_portability: Integer route graph and travel receipts portable; Godot movement and water effects are adapters.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: No canoe purchase required in baseline; edge stamina charged once, canceled preview is free.

concepts.title: Neighbor Chorus — consent-aware offline collaborative chores
concepts.novelty_audit: Village offers paid shifts and Builder plans NPC construction crews. This coordinates optional nonconstruction chores with NPC schedules, autonomy and fair settlements.
concepts.player_scenario: Invite two villagers to gather apples and prepare supper. One prefers cooking, another is busy; negotiate roles and share a transparent reward while retaining solo completion.
player_loop: Invite two villagers to gather apples and prepare supper. One prefers cooking, another is busy; negotiate roles and share a transparent reward while retaining solo completion. The player must receive visible feedback after every accepted choice and may inspect a persistent consequence journal.
simulation_rules: NPCs opt in based on schedule, skill and consent; declining never harms relationship and does not abandon required village job.
Each work step has unique receipt and bounded units; repeated commands never exceed task target.
Solo path always exists; shared compensation conserves gold and goods and never makes balances negative.
service_contracts: Village owns consent/schedules, Farming owns harvest inputs, Principal owns energy/inventory/save.
Coordinator owns project ledger only; B-008 retains exclusive construction labor.

controls.mouse_keyboard: E invites NPC, J opens chore planner, click roles, Enter confirms.
controls.gamepad: A talks, shoulder opens planner, D-pad selects roles, B exits.
controls.touch: Tap resident prompt, use three-card chore planner and explicit settle button.

Original friendly work audio motifs and readable contribution icons.

performance_budget.mobile: At most two rendered helpers, 12 simulated projects and simplified animation, scheduler <2ms/day.

Player and helpers complete exactly ten units after duplicates and save/reload.
Settlement consumes goods and pays rewards once with targeted NPC memory.
adversarial_tests: Reject unavailable helper, expired invitation, duplicate work, over-target progress and negative payout.
Helper cancels mid-project without trapping inventory or punishing player socially.
concepts.engine_portability: Project/consent/receipt state portable; Godot NPC choreography and UI are replaceable.

economy_and_resource_contract.refund: Invitation is free; supper consumes three apples once at settlement, failure leaves resources intact.
